This feature is meant for InstantSearch to not render anything until it receives some results, right? (only the first load the first time)
Yes, otherwise on the first `search` InstantSearch schedules a stalled render. If the delay is reached we call the render, but we don't have the results yet which throws an error.
should the default value of stalled search not be `false`?

Because of these changes the InstantSearch instance no longer has a `.widgets`, and that's why we can't do something like this:

```
instantsearch.widgets = [
  mainIndex [
    searchBox
    whatever
    index [
      something
    ]
  ]
  router
]
```

Or do I misunderstand something?

seems like this was from a previous PR, but what about:

```
mainHelper.search = mainHelper.searchOnlyWithDerivedHelpers
```
Which kind of warning would you give? "there's no need for this" or "it is wrong when you are using the index widget"?
where's this function called?
This clears all the cache since there's only one search client, so we should be fine :)
It needs to be stalled at first. See #2623.

Both are valid. Users probably don't have to access the `helper` on the instance. There are different ways to access it, connectors, widgets, events. The second is also valid because within a multi-index context the `helper` won't be the full picture of the state anymore.

Not sure I understood the statement. Indeed `.widgets` is not available anymore since it's now scoped under the "main" index. The schema provided is incorrect. The `router` has to be scoped under `index` otherwise it does not have access to the rest of the widgets.

Note that for compatibly purpose we can still expose it. I didn't do it by default because (I think) the usage of `.widget` isn't that common. We can mirror the value of the main index if required (like we do for the [`helper`](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/3893#discussion_r297712527)).

It is called on [`addWidget`](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/8881841f28240766dded1a49b3dcb89ef3565327/src/lib/index.ts#L106) & [`removeWidget`](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/8881841f28240766dded1a49b3dcb89ef3565327/src/lib/index.ts#L144) at the index level once the instance is started. An `index` widget could contain one (or many) index widgets. It means that all of them will trigger a new search. To avoid multiple searches we defer them to trigger only one.
Both are equivalent.
